faq: Do you use a tracking service or build my own?
Either. We can store events in your own database, or send them to tools such as PostHog, Mixpanel or Amplitude if you already use one. We recommend the simplest fit.
Is it allowed to track my users like this?
Product activity inside your own app is normal, but rules depend on your users' location. We record only what you need and give notes for your privacy policy. We do not give legal advice.
Will it slow my app down?
No. Events are sent in the background and batched, so screens stay quick. We check the effect before and after on a typical page.
Can I see activity from before this was built?
Only if you already store it somewhere, such as logs or an analytics tool. Otherwise it starts recording from launch day, and we make that clear in the handover.
desc:
User activity tracking views for SaaS support show what each person actually did in your product. Ecom Swift LLC builds timelines, usage trends and last-seen lists in your own app, so your team can answer questions quickly and spot users who have gone quiet.

## What are user activity views?

User activity views are screens that record and display actions inside your product. Support can open one account and see logins, key actions and errors in order, with times and devices. Product and success teams can see which features are used most and which users have not returned.

They sit between raw logs, which are hard to read, and full analytics tools, which are often more than a small team needs.

## Why activity views help support and retention

When a customer writes "it did not work", the first question is always what they did. Without a timeline, support asks for screenshots and steps, and the customer repeats themselves. With one, the agent can see the failed action, the error and the time, and often answer in one reply.

The same data helps you keep customers. A user who logs in less each week is showing a pattern, and a short note from your team at the right time can help. Feature usage trends show what people value and what nobody touches, which guides what to build or retire. We record only what is useful, and we follow your privacy policy.

## What good activity views include

- A defined list of key actions to record, such as sign-in, create, export and error.
- A timeline page for each user, newest first.
- Search by user email.
- Time and device shown for every event.
- A filter by action type.
- A feature usage chart by week.
- Lists of last seen and most active users.
- An account-level view across all users in a customer account.
- A simple engagement score that is easy to explain.
- Short privacy notes you can adapt for your policy.

## How we build it

We begin by agreeing which actions are worth recording. More is not better: each tracked event adds storage, privacy duties and noise. We choose the ones that answer your support and product questions.

Then we add the recording to your app's server, store events in a tidy structure and build the screens that read them. Your team sees a timeline, trends and lists inside your admin area, protected by admin-only access. The Basic package covers a handful of actions with a user timeline and email search. Standard adds more actions, usage charts, last-seen lists and filters. Premium adds account views, an engagement score and a weekly digest email. We design the recording to be light, so your app does not slow down for users.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Record actions that answer a real support or product question.
- Tell users what you collect in your privacy policy.
- Limit who on your team can open activity views.
- Keep personal details out of event data where possible.
- Set a retention period so old events are removed.

**Avoid:**
- Recording everything just in case.
- Storing passwords, payment details or message contents.
- Letting every staff member see every account.
- Judging a customer by a score without reading the timeline.
- Promising users that nothing is tracked when something is.

## Who this is for

This service suits SaaS support teams that spend too long finding out what a user did. It suits customer success managers who want to find quiet accounts early, and founders who want to know which features are used. It also suits products moving beyond a basic admin panel.

## What we need from you

Tell us which actions matter, who on your team will use the views and what your privacy policy says about data collection. Send a list of the common support questions you want answered.

Please give us developer or collaborator access to your code repository, plus a test database if you have one. We never need your passwords. Activity from before the build cannot be recreated unless your app already stored it. After you order, we reply with a short checklist and keep you updated until the views are ready.
